title: Developer Velocity Bootcamp: 15min Sprint Canvas (draft)
content:
Purpose

Quick experimental sketch for a compact, reproducible bootcamp that gets an engineer from zero to a validated client integration in ~15 minutes. Goal: maximize perceived velocity while instrumenting for real failure modes and cost signals. This is an intentionally small, testable artifact (not the final onboarding product).

Audience

- New engineers evaluating Redwood API for embedding/chat/generation flows
- Internal SDETs and Solutions Engineers who run quick proofs for customers
- Developer advocates running live 15-min walkthroughs

High-level constraints

- No more than 15 minutes for the happy path (30m with guided troubleshooting).
- Minimal local deps: Node 18+, Python 3.11 optional. Use curl-first approach.
- Use a tiny reference repo: 1 file per language for essential flow + one prompt set.
- Telemetry hooks: capture latency bucket, token delta, and first-error cause.
- Safety-first fallback: prebuilt trivial fallback text for network/429s.

Structure (Sprint Canvas)

1) Preflight (2 min)
- Sign up + copy API key (UI). Note: document the exact UI path and backups (CLI token export).
- Ensure local env var set: REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
- Quick sanity check: curl GET /v1/ping -> expect 200 and version string

2) Minimal happy path (7–9 min)
- Step A: Text generation smoke: curl POST /v1/generate with a 3-line prompt and streaming disabled. Show response tokens and time-of-first-byte measurement.
- Step B: Chat example: node single-file chat client that maintains a tiny message array and calls /v1/chat. Show how to surface function call responses (if any).
- Step C: Embeddings quick query: python one-liner that creates two 768-embedding vectors and computes cosine similarity locally.

3) Observability + cost check (1–2 min)
- Inspect dashboard link (token-level sample) for request just made.
- Show cost estimation: token count * sample rate -> approximate cost.

4) Failure and recovery (2–4 min)
- Induce a 429 by hitting an intentionally small burst script (explain safety rules) and show fallback behavior.
- Simulate long-tail latency: set client timeout to 2s and show graceful retry -> fallback to smaller-model variant via policy header.

5) Next steps & handoff (remaining time)
- Save snippet into repo, link to templates.
- Prompt hygiene quick checklist: anchor instructions, expected schema, example outputs.
- Add to project board: small ticket to instrument a dedicated telemetry metric for that route.

Reference assets to include in kit

- repo: /templates/bootcamp/15min/{curl,js,py} (1-file examples)
- one-page cheat sheet (single PDF) with commands + recovery steps
- short video (90s) showing the five steps (for advocates)
- telemetry manifest: set of spans and labels to emit (latency_buckets, token_delta, error_reason)

Minimal code examples (TO BE INCLUDED IN REPO)

- curl example (happy path)
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rw-bert-small-1","input":"Write a 3-line haiku about debugging"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

- Node single-file chat (pseudocode)
  // chat-quick.js
  // single dependency: node fetch builtin
  const messages = [{role:"system",content:"You are a helpful assistant."}, {role:"user",content:"Summarize our meeting notes"}];
  fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', {method:'POST', headers:{'Authorization':`Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`}, body: JSON.stringify({model:'rw-chat-mini', messages})})
    .then(r=>r.json()).then(console.log).catch(e=>console.error('call failed', e));

Telemetry & Measurement (design notes, not final)

- Required captured labels per call: route, model, tokens_input, tokens_output, latency_ms, status_code, error_class
- Lightweight client libraries should emit a single event per call with these labels (JSON over UDP or HTTP batched).
- For 15-min playbooks, aggregate: p50/p95 latencies, token distribution, and percent of sessions that hit fallback.

Safety and fallback patterns (practical)

- Local timeout -> fail fast, provide cached or canned response for demo. Keep fallback text short and clearly labelled as fallback.
- Rate limit -> instruct demo runner to switch to 'demo-key' which maps to higher burst limits. Avoid telling customers to use production keys for demos.
- Prompt-anchoring -> demonstrate using an explicit 'Do not hallucinate' instruction + schema enforcement.

Open design questions (notes to self)

- Do we want the minimal examples to ship with a tiny local mock server that simulates 429s/latency? Tradeoff: more setup vs consistent demo.
- How aggressive should the telemetry be for an opt-in quickstart? We want useful signal but low noise and privacy-safe defaults.
- Should we make a single-file 'panic-button' script that switches routing headers to fallback variants? (useful for advocates)

Quick checklist for the demo runner (one-liner tasks)

- [ ] Confirm account has demo_key with burst limit 30rps
- [ ] Export REDWOOD_API_KEY into shell
- [ ] Open dashboard link to the live project (tab 1)
- [ ] Run curl sanity check (tab 2)
- [ ] Execute node chat file and show console output (tab 2)
- [ ] Show telemetry spike on dashboard within 10s
- [ ] Trigger and recover from a simulated 429 (tab 2)

Low-effort followups if this goes well

- Add language: Go and Ruby 1-file examples (low priority)
- Create a step-by-step Notion page with screenshots and alt text (for less technical audiences)
- Small PR to SDK repo: telemetry shim that emits the required labels by default

Notes / Unpolished fragments (work-in-progress)

- "If user sees 'empty response', check keys and model compatibility (embedding vs text)"
- "Consider a short non-technical explainer for sales: 'what to expect in a 15 minute Redwood demo'"
- "We should avoid shipping the demo with hard-coded production-looking data that could confuse customers"

Action items (initial)

- Asha: create template repo with three files + README (2 days)
- Miguel: prototype a tiny mockserver that can inject latency and 429s (3 days)
- Evelyn: draft short video script and 90s recording plan (1 week)
- Jonah: add telemetry manifest and Linear ticket for metric collection (2 days)

Last thoughts

This canvas is intentionally small so we can iterate fast. The magic is in the automation: one-click provisioning of 'demo_key', a repo with minimal examples, and an advocate video that reduces cognitive friction. Keep it simple, surface the observability we care about, and capture those signals so Product and Infra can see how real teams experience the flow.
